subject: Cannot debug "rejecting initial value" with print?

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Cannot debug "rejecting initial value" with print?
parts:
I have a model that isn't even getting started; it fails with a bunch of messages saying "Rejecting initial value: Log probability evaluates to log(0)..." To debug it, I sprinkled print statements all throughout the model block. None of these print statements ever executes. I know that print works -- I put a print statement in the transformed data block, and I see the output. But, apparently, Stan never gets to the model block.

How is Stan concluding that the log prob evaluates to log(0) without ever entering the code that actually computes the log prob?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cannot debug "rejecting initial value" with print?
parts:
All you can do is replace the multi_normal statement with something
that does not depend on sigbeta and then the print statements will be
output, but you also won’t get the right Markov chain.

But if sigbeta is really diagonal then you don’t need the multi_normal
at all as the multivariate normal decouples into a product of independent
univariate normal distributions.  In that case you can just take advantage
of the vectorization of the univariate normal,

beta ~ normal(0, betawd);

Of course if sigbeta wasn’t positive definite then some of those betawd
are ill-defined and you’ll have have problems.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cannot debug "rejecting initial value" with print?
parts:
It might be as soon as two months. There was a lot
of stuff that got pushed back just past 2.10.

- Bob

> On Jul 6, 2016, at 6:16 AM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> There is no workaround without modified the underlying code. If you can’t
> get to the develop branch then you’ll have to wait for the next official release
> which won’t be for at least a few months.
>
> On Jul 6, 2016, at 12:08 PM, Jonathan Harris <jgha...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>> Probably won't work. I am trying this on a corporate computer, so I am greatly restricted. I can't even access most Github sites, including the Stan one.
>>
>>
>> On Tuesday, July 5, 2016 at 10:26:14 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
>> Almost -- there's an open pull request to deal with it now:
>> https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/1938
>>
>> If you are using CmdStan, you can update the submodule for Stan to the branch there, rebuild CmdStan and your Stan program, and then you'll see print output.
>>
>>
>> Daniel
>>
>>
>> On Tue, Jul 5, 2016 at 10:05 PM, Jonathan Harris <jgha...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> I am having this problem also. Is there a workaround? It is awfully hard to find out why my covvariance matrix is not positive definite if I cannot print intermediate values!
>>
>>
>> On Monday, March 7, 2016 at 12:57:36 AM UTC-5, Kevin Van Horn wrote:
>> I have a model that isn't even getting started; it fails with a bunch of messages saying "Rejecting initial value: Log probability evaluates to log(0)..." To debug it, I sprinkled print statements all throughout the model block. None of these print statements ever executes. I know that print works -- I put a print statement in the transformed data block, and I see the output. But, apparently, Stan never gets to the model block.
>>
>> How is Stan concluding that the log prob evaluates to log(0) without ever entering the code that actually computes the log prob?
>>
